title: JSON number masking runs in linear time on long digit runs

change.what: maskJsonNumberTokens runs one module-level sticky number regex (the same pattern, flag y) with lastIndex set to index, instead of the anchored regex on text.slice(index). When a match fails the start or end boundary check, the whole matched span is appended unchanged and the scan continues at its end; with no match one character is appended as before. The function is now exported so the test can compare it with a copy of the old one.
change.unchanged: The number pattern, both boundary checks, quote and escape tracking, the normalisation, redactPrivateText and every other rule.

equalityArgument: The number pattern only matches the characters 0-9, '-', '+', '.', 'e' and 'E', so a matched span holds no quote: the quoted state cannot change inside it.

The old code, after a failed boundary check at index, appended text[index] and tried each later position j in the span. Every such j follows a span character, which is not whitespace, ':', '[' or ',', so a number starting at j fails the start check; a j whose character is not '-' or a digit is appended without a match.
So the old code appended every character of the span unchanged and reached its end in the same state; the new code appends the span in one step.
The pattern cannot match the empty string, so the scan always advances.

benchmark.shape: redactDerivative on '[' + N digits '7' + 'x', best of 3 after a warm-up call, this PC, Node 24.19.0

tests.linear: Three 64 KiB shapes after '[' and before 'x' (digits; '12-3.4' repeated; '9-1.5e3-' repeated), one timed redactDerivative call each, each under 100 ms (whole test 13 to 14 ms).
tests.equal: maskJsonNumberTokens compared with a copy of the old function on 26 hand-picked and 2000 seeded generated test_only strings (signs, decimals, exponents, leading zeros, numbers beside quotes, brackets, commas, colons and letters, escaped quotes and backslashes inside strings, unclosed strings): all 2026 equal, 168 changed by masking (at least 150 asserted).
